slides.text:
A conditional runs code only when a condition is true. In Go the condition must be a `bool`, it has no parentheses, and the braces are always required.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
if the condition is true
    do this
otherwise if another is true
    do that
otherwise
    do the other

exercises.title: If and else
exercises.guide: Choose between two paths with `if` and `else`.

chunks.guide: The block after `if` runs when the condition is true. Otherwise the block after `else` runs.
This line runs after the `if`, whichever path was taken.

exercises.title: Why does it not compile?
exercises.guide: Read the message, then pick the cause.
exercises.code:
./main.go:7:17: syntax error:
  unexpected newline, expected { after
  if clause
options: The `{` must stay on the `if` line
exercises.explanation: Go ends a line without a `{` as a complete statement. The opening brace goes on the same line as the `if`.

exercises.title: Several choices
exercises.guide: Pick one of three paths with an `else if` chain.

chunks.guide: The conditions are checked from the top. The first true one runs its block, and the rest are skipped. `else` catches what is left.

notes.text: Tried only if the checks above were false.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `n > 5` is true, so its block runs and the chain stops there. `n > 10` is never checked.

exercises.title: A variable for the if
exercises.guide: Declare a variable inside the `if` line itself.

chunks.guide: An `if` can start with a short statement, then a `;`, then the condition. `rem` exists only inside the `if` and its `else`.

notes.text: Runs first, before the condition is checked.

chunks.guide: `rem` is gone here, but `total` is still in scope.

exercises.title: What kind of error is it?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the kind of error.
exercises.explanation: An `if` needs a `bool`. Go has no truthy numbers, so write `count != 0` or `count > 0`.
